summary: Two placebo-controlled RCTs of the exact Sensoril root-and-leaf extract: 27647541 (60 adults with knee pain, 250 or 500 mg/day for 12 weeks) improved the primary modified WOMAC outcome (p<0.001 at 500 mg/day, p<0.05 at 250 mg/day); 38732539 (131 chronically stressed adults, 98 per-protocol, 125-500 mg/day for 8 weeks) lowered the primary PSS and cortisol/ACTH/amylase markers versus placebo. Both are credited within their populations, with small-sample and attrition limits kept.

applicability.studied_population: Adults 20-58 with self-reported chronic stress taking Sensoril 125-500 mg/day for 8 weeks (PMID 38732539).

identity.standardization: Aqueous root-and-leaf Withania somnifera extract, >=10% withanolide glycosides, >=32% oligosaccharides, <=0.5% withaferin A (HPLC)

population.description: 60 adults aged 40-70 (43 men, 17 women; mean 57.8 y) with knee joint pain and discomfort for at least 6 months, ARA functional class I-III and baseline VAS pain >=40 mm; 20 per arm, after a 7-10 day analgesic washout.

study_contexts.study_design: Prospective randomized double-blind placebo-controlled three-arm parallel trial (125 mg or 250 mg twice daily vs placebo), 12 weeks.

outcomes.name: Primary: percentage change in modified WOMAC at 12 weeks: significant reduction vs placebo with 250 mg twice daily (p<0.001) and 125 mg twice daily (p<0.05)
Knee Swelling Index and VAS pain, stiffness and disability at 12 weeks: significant reductions in both Sensoril arms; 250 mg arm showed earliest change (4 weeks, within-group)

limitations: Small single-centre trial (n=60) analysed with t-tests/ANOVA on mean change; paracetamol 650 mg rescue permitted.
Knee joint pain/discomfort population; not established osteoarthritis disease modification. Exact Sensoril root-and-leaf material; no transfer to other ashwagandha extracts.
Early (4- and 8-week) comparisons are within-group versus baseline, not placebo-adjusted onset.
Returned decision A020: source-content hold; methods verified from full text.

Dr. Pham's fourth ruling set (2026-10-28): exact Sensoril standardized root-and-leaf aqueous extract (root+leaf is correct for Sensoril; no root-only requirement), studied outcome and applicable population only; no transfer to generic ashwagandha powder.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.
Not credit-bearing: Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling limits Sensoril credit to the studied stress outcome; the earlier knee decision (A020) was a hold.

dose.administration_frequency: One capsule (125 mg or 250 mg) twice daily after food.
co_therapies: Source-reported concurrent-care/restriction context: Patients who discontinued all current analgesic therapy, including NSAIDs, over the counter pain medications and topical analgesics for 7–10 days prior to the start of the study were randomized into the study.

Source-reported concurrent-care/restriction context: A run-in period was allowed between screening visit (Visit 1) and randomization visit (Visit 2) to ensure that the were weaned off all medications 7–10 days prior to randomization.
Source-reported concurrent-care/restriction context: Paracetamol 650 mg tablets were used as and when required as rescue medication.

Source-reported concurrent-care/restriction context: The study and rescue medications were dispensed at visits 2, 3 and 4 and compliance to study medications was checked by pill count method during the subsequent visits.
dose.reported_regimen: Sensoril 125 mg or 250 mg capsule twice daily (250 or 500 mg/day) or identical placebo for 12 weeks.

normalization.basis: Capsule strength x 2 daily = 250 or 500 mg/day Sensoril extract as assigned.

source_provenance.location: Methods (inclusion criteria; study medication Sensoril composition; run-in; primary outcome mWOMAC % change at 12 weeks); Results Table 2(a), Fig. 3

identity.standardization: Aqueous root-and-leaf Withania somnifera extract, chemically characterized (50 small molecules identified)

population.description: 131 community-dwelling adults with self-reported high chronic stress (PSS criterion), mean age 35 (range 20-58), excluding major medical/psychiatric disorders and recent psychotropic or nutraceutical use; 98 per-protocol (70 men, 28 women).

study_contexts.study_design: 8-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel-group trial of three Sensoril doses (125, 250, 500 mg/day) vs placebo; CTRI/2019/11/022100; per-protocol linear mixed models.

outcomes.name: Primary: 14-item Perceived Stress Scale: all three doses significantly decreased PSS vs placebo at 8 weeks (between-group p<0.001 at week 8); dose-dependent differences
Primary biochemical stress markers: salivary alpha-amylase, plasma cortisol and ACTH lower than placebo in all extract groups; DHEA-S unchanged
HAM-A and HAM-D lower vs placebo at weeks 2-8

limitations: High attrition: 131 enrolled, 98 per-protocol; no intention-to-treat efficacy analysis and no multiplicity adjustment.
Printed enrolment sex counts total 111 versus 131 enrolled; reporting discrepancy retained.
Healthy adults with mild-to-moderate self-reported stress; not anxiety-disorder or depression treatment. Exact Sensoril material only.
Returned decision A020: source-content hold; methods verified from full text.

Dr. Pham's fourth ruling set (2026-10-28): exact Sensoril standardized root-and-leaf aqueous extract (root+leaf is correct for Sensoril; no root-only requirement), studied outcome and applicable population only; no transfer to generic ashwagandha powder.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: One capsule at night, about 30 minutes before bedtime.
co_therapies: No concurrent psychotropic or nutraceutical medication permitted (exclusion criteria).
dose.reported_regimen: Single Sensoril capsule nightly providing 125, 250 or 500 mg/day, or matching placebo, for 8 weeks.

normalization.basis: One capsule per day containing the assigned 125, 250 or 500 mg of Sensoril extract.

source_provenance.location: Methods 2.1-2.4 (design, participants, intervention, primary outcome); Results 3.1-3.2, Tables 1-3, Figure 2
